sources.quote: equilibrium wage will be a (σ −1)/σ% change. In the plausible case where σ < 1, this is

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: negative. The overall impact may still be an increase in wages because of the productivity

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: effect, but as already noted, when σ is approximately equal to the share of capital in national

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: income, the overall impact will be essentially zero. In conclusion, without the creation of a

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: sufficient number of new tasks, inequality between capital and labor will increase and wage

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: rises may be limited.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: What about a reduction in inequality because lower-skill workers benefit more? In the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: model here, the earnings of high-skill workers relative to low-skill workers is always pinned

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: down at λH/λU. So if new technologies reduce this ratio, they will reduce the gap between

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: high-skill and low-skill workers. But even this conclusion needs to be qualified. Acemoglu and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: Restrepo (2022) show that in more general settings, with multiple skill groups, there will be

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: ripple effects whereby impacted demographic groups can then compete for tasks previously

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: performed by other groups. In such a situation, an overall increase in labor productivity

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: of both high-skill and low-skill workers in some tasks can lead to their displacement from

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: these tasks, and then the ripple effects can, in principle, affect low-skill workers even more

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: adversely than high-skill workers.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: While such adverse effects on low-skill workers are a general possibility in the framework

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: of Acemoglu and Restrepo (2022), I am not aware of worked-out examples where an increase

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 23 页
sources.quote: in the productivity of low-skill workers increases inequality. I now provide such an example.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote:
2.10
How Greater Low-Skill Productivity Can Lead to Higher In-
equality

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: Let me illustrate this possibility with a simple example, by relaxing the assumption that there

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: are no comparative advantage differences between high-skill and low-skill workers. Suppose

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: that the economy starts from an equilibrium in which tasks below some I are performed

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: by capital, and tasks between I and N are performed by a combination of high-skill and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: low-skill workers. In particular, suppose that low-skill workers have a comparative advantage

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: in tasks between I and I∗, and denote their (constant) productivity in these tasks by λU,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: while the productivity of high-skill workers in these tasks is also constant and equal to λH.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: Suppose also that the relative productivity of high-skill workers in tasks between I∗and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: N is ω > λH/λU—indicating that high-skill workers have a comparative advantage in higher-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: indexed tasks. However, because there is no strict comparative advantage, the equilibrium

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: may involve both types of workers performing some of the same tasks.19 Assume also that

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: the elasticity of substitution between tasks is σ < 1.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: Let us start with an equilibrium in which both high-skill and low-skill workers perform

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: tasks z ∈(I, I∗], while only high-skill workers perform tasks z ∈(I∗, N]. In this initial equi-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: librium, the relative wage of skilled workers will be pinned down by the relative productivities

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: of the two types of workers in the tasks they are both performing—i.e., z ∈(I, I∗]—and is

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: given by λH/λU.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: Suppose that labor productivity in z ∈(I, I∗] increases due to advances in AI, and this

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote:
also is more helpful for lower-skilled workers, and so λH/λU declines.
I now show that

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: these advances could boost inequality. Because σ < 1, the prices of tasks z ∈(I, I∗] will

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: decline more than the increase in physical productivity of labor, and there will be less labor

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: assigned to these tasks. If this effect is significant, all high-skill workers may be allocated

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: away from these tasks, and the amount of labor demanded in these tasks may fall short of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: the supply of low-skill workers. In this case, the post-AI allocation may involve only low-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: skill workers performing tasks z ∈(I, I∗], while both low-skill and high-skill workers perform

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: tasks z ∈(I∗, N]. Then, regardless of how much λH/λU declines, the relative wage of skilled

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: workers will be determined by the tasks that both types of workers are performing, which

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote: are now those above I∗, and thus will be equal to ω > λH/λU. Hence, inequality increases

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 24 页
sources.quote:
19This structure makes the example similar to one that has a finite number of tasks—in this instance,
three tasks. But I use the setting with a continuum of tasks for continuity with the rest of the paper. The
“paradoxical” result I am highlighting here does not depend on this stark structure or on having just two
types of labor.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: following the rise in the productivity of low-skill workers.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: Therefore, I have just proven that, in this general scenario, even a reduced productivity

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: gap between low-skill and high-skill workers in some tasks could lead to greater inequality.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: Hence, the overall inequality implications of AI cannot be directly deduced from its effects

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: on the performance of workers of different skills in a given set of tasks and requires a fuller

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: empirical exploration. In the next section, I investigate AI’s inequality effects by adapting

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: the framework and estimates of Acemoglu and Restrepo (2022) to the current setting.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote:
3
A Preliminary Quantitative Evaluation

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: In this section, I provide a preliminary quantitative evaluation of the possible effects of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote:
recent breakthroughs in AI over a horizon of 10 years.
The centerpiece will be the use

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: of Hulten’s theorem and recent estimates of which tasks can be automated using AI and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: computer vision technologies and the cost savings thereof. Once I obtain these estimates

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: from Hulten’s theorem for TFP growth, I convert them to GDP growth estimates using

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: another series of assumptions on how the capital stock of the economy will respond. I also

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: discuss AI’s effects through new bad tasks could be estimated. Finally, I combine these

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: numbers with the more detailed framework in Acemoglu and Restrepo (2022) to obtain

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: even more speculative estimates for wage and inequality implications. Before moving to the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: estimates, I first describe the sources I use, further discuss existing productivity estimates

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: and motivate various parameter choices.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote:
3.1
Data Sources and Parameter Choices

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: The centerpiece of the estimates in this paper is equation (14), and its refinement to (15).

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: To implement this equation, two pieces of information are needed:

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: 1. GDP share of tasks that are impacted by AI (inclusive of computer vision) within the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: next 10 years.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: 2. Average cost savings in these tasks due to AI, ¯π.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: It is impossible to have accurate estimates of either of these two quantities, and hence

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: my repeated caution that the numbers here—and for that matter, other estimates in the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: literature and the public debate—should be interpreted with great caution as suggestive

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: numbers. Nevertheless, there are studies that have already shed light on these quantities. I

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 25 页
sources.quote: now discuss what these are and how I use them.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: GDP Share of Tasks Impacted by AI

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: The most careful estimates of which tasks are exposed to recent AI and computer vision

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: advances come from Eloundou et al. (2023). These authors use two related methodologies

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: for classifying which tasks are exposed to AI and computer vision. Both of those start from

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: O*NET task and Detailed Work Activity (DWA) descriptions. The authors ask GPT-4 to

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: classify all 19,265 tasks and 2,087 DWAs. They also develop a coarser index by manually

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: classifying DWAs and then cross-validating their GPT-based measure with this “human”

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote:
coding.
Here, I focus on the GPT-based measure which allows greater granularity, as I

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: explain next. In addition, Eloundou et al. (2023) distinguish between a direct exposure

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: (α) measure, which is based on their assessment of what large language models (LLMs)

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: can achieve now. They then develop a second, more aggressive measure (their so-called β

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: measure), allowing “indirect” exposure to a hypothetical LLM+. This includes tasks that

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: will be (possibly) exposed to new software and other advances building on current LLM and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: computer vision technologies.20

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: The index Eloundou et al. report in the paper is based on a binary coding, while they

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: also construct an “automation” index, and in this case their β measure includes granular

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: information about what fraction of the activities might be impacted by LLM+ (ranging

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: across 0%, 25%, 50%, 75% and 100%). In what follows, I take their automation index to be

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: able to use this granular information. This index still contains both automation and task

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: complementarities, even if it emphasizes automation a little more than their other exposure

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: indices (because they code the granular information on the basis of information about what

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: activities can be automated). In particular, as the authors themselves note, the impact

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: of generative AI may often involve automation of some subtasks, allowing human workers

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: to focus on other activities. The granular information contained in this index is especially

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: useful for my purposes, because it provides an assessment of which tasks/occupations are

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: less likely to be impacted by AI. I set all tasks that the authors classify as having 50% or

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: less of their activities impacted by AI and computer vision to zero, and I refer to the rest as

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: “AI exposed tasks”.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: There are several problems that need to be tackled to turn these estimates into the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote: quantities I need.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote:  Although Eloundou et al.’s automation index emphasizes automation, it still includes

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 26 页
sources.quote:
20They also report a third, even more aggressive measure, which they refer to as ζ.
This measure is
more speculative and focuses on what can be ultimately performed by LLM+. In line with the authors’
interpretation, this is unlikely to be the case in the near future, and I ignore this third measure.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: elements of “augmentation” or task complementarity. This motivates my interpretation

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: that combining their measure with equation (14) will capture cost savings from both

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: automation and task complementarities.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote:  Eloundou et al.’s data need to be converted into GDP shares. To do this, I com-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: bine tasks into occupations, and then I aggregate across occupations using their wage

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: bills, computed from the US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) National Occupational

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: Employment and Wage Estimates pooled across the years 2019-2022. This procedure

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: yields a wage bill-weighted share of exposed occupations equal to 20%. I interpret this

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: number to be the same as the GDP share of tasks exposed to AI.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote:  Eloundou et al.’s approach is to determine tasks that can be ultimately performed

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: by generative AI and computer vision technologies (such as the technology already

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: incorporated in Dall-E). Two things are missing from the information they provide.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: The first is how much of the task impact is likely to be realized within the next 10 years.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: The second is whether, in all of these cases, it is profitable to use AI (e.g., whether

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: automating using AI is cost-effective). Svanberg et al. (2024) make an attempt to

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: provide answers to these questions in the case of computer vision technologies, which

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: are a subset of the technologies Eloundou et al. consider. I take Svanberg et al.’s

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: estimates and extrapolate them to all of the tasks Eloundou et al. consider.21 Namely,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: Svanberg et al.’s base estimates imply that among computer vision-exposed tasks, 23%

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: can be feasibly (and profitably) automated within 10 years.22 Applying this number to

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: Eloundou et al.’s estimates, I arrive at the GDP share of tasks impacted by AI within

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: the next 10 years as 0.23 × 0.200 = 4.6% of all tasks (or occupations).

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: Cost Savings from AI

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: I base my estimate of ¯π on the experimental studies that have already provided “proof-of-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote: concept” estimates of productivity improvements or labor cost reductions due to AI. Three

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote:
21This is not an innocuous step. Svanberg et al. focus on automation using computer vision, while Eloun-
dou et al.’s exposed technologies include task complementarities as noted above and go beyond computer
vision tasks. One could imagine that the share of tasks that can be profitably used with AI within 10 years
is different between these two categories. Unfortunately, I do not have another source for such an estimate
for non-computer vision AI.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 27 页
sources.quote:
22Svanberg et al. also make further extrapolations assuming cost declines in computer vision technologies.
They base these on estimates from Besiroglu and Hobbhahn (2022), who project a 22% yearly decrease in
computation costs attributed to the expansion of compute power from GPUs. However, a doubling of GPU
capacity will not necessarily translate into a 50% decline in costs in general due to diminishing returns and
bottlenecks created by other inputs, and because of the limitation of the current architecture. I therefore do
not include these in the baseline but return to them in the robustness discussion.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: studies, which I have already mentioned, are particularly notable here, and I now describe

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: each one of them.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote:  Peng et al. (2023) design an experiment where freelance computer programmers are

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: given access to and encouraged to use GitHub Copilot, which (at the time of the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: experiment) was powered by OpenAI Codex (GPT-3). Participants were given the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: task of implementing a HTTP server on JavaScript, a popular language for which

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: resources and subroutines are readily available, and GPT-3 was already trained on these

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: resources. They compare the experimental treatment group to a control group that is

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: not given access to GitHub Copilot. They find that the treatment group performed

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: the assigned tasks on average 55.8% faster than the control group. As an aside, like

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: the other studies I mention here, Peng et al. find that these improvements come from

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: otherwise less well-performing subjects.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote:  Noy and Zhang (2023) design an online experiment where individuals in a range of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: white-collar occupations are recruited and presented with simple writing tasks (in

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: particular, tasks like writing press releases, short reports and analyses that are designed

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: to take 20 to 30 minutes and resemble real life tasks in the participants’ occupations).

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: The treatment group is given access to and encouraged to use ChatGPT-3.5, while the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: control group is not. They verify that there is very low usage of ChatGPT in the control

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: group. They estimate that ChatGPT enables, on average, 40% faster completion of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: the task at hand. They also estimate an 18% improvement in quality scores, as judged

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: by peers and ChatGPT-based scoring of the output. In their case, too, the gains come

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: mostly from subjects that performed less well before the experiment.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote:  Brynjolfsson et al. (2023) is the only study that I am aware of that looks at the use of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: generative AI tools in a real business setting with a careful experimental design. The

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: business they focus on is a customer service provider, which uses a custom generative

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: AI tool to help customer service associates. The rollout took the form of a treatment

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: group getting access to this tool, while the control group did not. Brynjolfsson, Li

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: and Raymond evaluate the impact of the rollout on cost savings, by focusing on how

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: quickly tasks (open customer tickets) are resolved. They also look at self-reported

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: customer satisfaction. They find a significant improvement in the speed with which

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: tasks are completed by customer service associates—an effect of about 14% on average.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 28 页
sources.quote: However, they additionally estimate a slight and statistically insignificant decline in

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: quality, as judged by the users themselves. Like the other studies, Brynjolfsson, Li and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: Raymond find that the results are predominantly among the lower-performing, less

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: expert employees. In fact, they estimate that the top quintile of associates experience

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: no improvement at all.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: I interpret all three studies as providing labor cost savings from AI, broadly construed—in

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: particular, meaning that all three studies include both automation and task complementarity

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: elements. For instance, for the GitHub Copilot users in Peng et al., the authors’ interpreta-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: tion is that some of the subtasks previously performed by programmers, such as the writing

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote:
of common routines, are now done by the Copilot.
Along the lines of the discussion in

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: Section 2.2, suppose that programming in JavaScript involves N subtasks, which need to

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: be completed for a successful program. These include initial planning (which approach to

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: adopt, how to organize the program, etc.), composition of subroutines, putting the subrou-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: tines together, debugging the subroutines, debugging the master program and then assessing

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: whether the program achieves the planned aims. When all of these subtasks are performed,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: then the task at hand—the writing of a specific computer program—is completed. We can

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: think of generative AI as taking over a subset of the composition of subroutine tasks. Then

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: in line with the framework in Acemoglu and Restrepo (2018, 2019b), the use of this new

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: technology will create displacement and productivity effects. Overall performance will in-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: crease because of productivity effects, provided that this technology is better than/faster

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: than humans at composing some subroutines (but humans are still needed for the other sub-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: tasks, including planning, debugging and checking). Demand for human labor in this task

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: may increase or decrease depending on the magnitude of the displacement and productivity

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: effects and the elasticity of substitution between this task and other tasks (as well as the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: demand elasticity for the product that is ultimately being produced for the market). In

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: addition, when simple subroutines are taken over by the Copilot, this may enable human

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: workers to specialize in other subtasks, potentially generating task complementarities and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: further productivity gains.23

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: What I have just described for programming also applies to the other two studies. Chat-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote: GPT is doing some of the drafting, which human subjects can then take and incorporate into

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 29 页
sources.quote:
23However, in this experimental setting, we do not see the displacement effects, because each of the
treatment subjects are given the task and there is no possibility of reducing the number of workers performing
this task.
Hence, from these experiments, we can only learn about the productivity gains, inclusive of
any task complementarities—and not about the displacement effects. This interpretation clarifies why I
am comfortable bundling automation and task complementarities together for the purposes of estimating
productivity gains from AI.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: their writing with some verification and modification. The same applies for the customer

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: service associates, who are allowed to copy and paste text suggested by the generative AI

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: tool in the setting studied by Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: I also assess that the tasks in these three studies are broadly comparable to the exposed

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: tasks considered in Eloundou et al. (2023), even though I argue later that they are more

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: likely to be in the easy-to-learn category. Hence, these studies are most informative about

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: cost savings (productivity improvements) for the exposed tasks in Eloundou et al.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: As a baseline, I ignore the quality effects (which, as noted, are not uniform between

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: the three studies) and focus on the average increase in speed and interpret this as average

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: cost savings. I return to the inequality implications below. Finally, as a baseline, I use the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: average of the estimates from Noy and Zhang (2023) and Brynjolfsson et al. (2023), and turn

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: to the average of the three studies as a robustness check. The reason for this is that Peng

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: et al.’s setting is less likely to be relevant to other tasks and occupations, since the task in

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: question is a very well-defined one for which Github Copilot was extensively trained, and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: this has no direct equivalent in the other tasks we are focusing on. Under these assumptions,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: the average labor cost savings are 27% (= 0.27).

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: Recall that these numbers refer to declines in labor costs in occupations, where many

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: tasks involve use both capital and labor, and what is relevant in equation (14) is overall

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: cost savings. To convert labor cost savings into overall cost savings, I use the industry-level

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote:
estimates from Eloundou et al.
and combine them with industry labor shares from the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA), as described in the Appendix.24 This gives an average

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: (AI exposure-adjusted) labor share of 0.535, and thus the average (overall) cost savings from

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: If we add the numbers from Peng et al. to the mix, the average labor cost savings become

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote: 0.36, and thus the average overall cost savings come to 0.193.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 30 页
sources.quote:
24Briefly, I follow Eloundou et al. and map exposed tasks to occupations, and then map occupations to 14
aggregated NIPA (National Income and Product Accounts) industries using the fractions of workers in each
occupation employed across industries. I then compute the labor share of exposed tasks using industry labor
shares weighted by the value-added shares of these industries in gross national income. In these calculations,
the self-employed are assumed to have the same hourly wage rate as employees in the same industry. I
use the 14 NIPA industries to be able to have information on hours worked. These data are for the years
2018-2022 from the US BEA NIPA tables, and I provide a list of these 14 industries in the Appendix.
For reference, the average (value-added-weighted) labor share in 2018-2022, without the exposure adjust-
ment, is 0.576. This suggests that exposed tasks are, on average, in industries with slightly lower labor shares
than the national average. This labor share estimate is similar to the one reported in Elsby et al. (2013),
0.583, for private non-farm business sector for the years 2010-2012 using the same approach as here. Elsby
et al. (2013) also report similar numbers under alternative methodologies for incorporating self-employment
income.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote:
3.2
Aggregate Productivity Gains: A First Pass

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: A first-pass estimate of productivity (TFP) gains at the aggregate level can be obtained

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: simply by combining the numbers derived in the previous subsection with equation (14).

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: This implies:

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote:
TFP gains over 10 years
=
GDP share impacted by AI over the next 10 years

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: × average cost savings of impact tasks.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: Therefore, on the basis of the numbers from the previous subsection, I can approximate:

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote:
TFP gains over the next 10 years
=
0.046 × 0.144

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: In other words, according to this basic estimation strategy, TFP gains over the next 10 years

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: from AI are about 0.66%—meaning that relative to the baseline without the current suite of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: AI and computer vision advances, TFP will be higher by 0.66 percentage points in 10 years,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: or annual TFP growth will be higher by around 0.064%. This is a nontrivial, but modest

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: effect, and certainly much less than both the revolutionary changes some are predicting and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: the less hyperbolic but still substantial improvements forecast by Goldman Sachs and the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: McKinsey Global Institute, which I discussed in the Introduction.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: If we were to consider the higher productivity numbers from Peng et al., 0.144 would be

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: replaced by 0.193, and the 10-year TFP gains would be 0.89%, instead of 0.66%.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: The only modification that would make a sizable difference to these numbers is to increase

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: the fraction of tasks that will be impacted over the next 10 years. One way of doing this

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: is to inflate the numbers from Svanberg et al.. This could be because either the fraction of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: tasks that can be feasibly automated will be different for generative AI than for computer

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: vision, or because within 10 years this fraction will increase significantly. For example, in

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: Svanberg et al.’s scenarios where costs for computer vision decline very rapidly, such as 10%

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: a year, the fraction of tasks that are feasibly automated may be as high as 30%. This would

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: raise the GDP share impacted by AI to approximately 6%, and correspondingly increase

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: the TFP gains over the next 10 years to about 0.9%. Note that even this number is quite

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: modest, and moreover, 10% per annum cost declines is quite aggressive (since, as already

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: noted above, even if GPU costs were to decrease by 10% or even 20%, this would not lead

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: to a 10% decline in costs of performing computer vision tasks, given the presence of other

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: inputs, such as programming and data, as well as the inherent limitations of the current

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 31 页
sources.quote: generative AI architecture).

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: Finally, I note three important considerations missing from these computations.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: 1. These adoption numbers ignore the fact that there is still very little investment in AI

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: in the US corporate sector. Acemoglu et al. (2022) estimate that less than 1.5% of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: US businesses had any investment in AI in 2019, and this is particularly true beyond

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: the very large companies in manufacturing, information services and business services.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: Since many of the tasks considered in Eloundou et al. (2023) are performed in small

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote:
and medium-sized enterprises, this is unlikely to change quickly.
If generative AI

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: tools become monopolized in the hands of a few companies, this might further slow

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: down their adoption by small and medium-sized firms. These considerations suggest

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: that even the 0.046% number for the share of GDP impacted by AI may be a big

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: overestimate, and the true numbers could be much smaller.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: 2. Any major technology creates adjustment costs when adopted at large scale, because

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: other organizational aspects need to evolve as well and this is typically quite costly

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: and slow. In the context of digital technologies, Greenwood and Yorukoglu (1997) and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: Brynjolfsson et al. (2021), among others, have argued that productivity gains will take

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: a J-shaped pattern, and the former paper predicts that the flat part of the J-curve lasts

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: no less than 20 years for digital technologies. If so, the 14.4% overall cost reductions

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: may be a significant overestimate for the next 10 years.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: 3. As already discussed above, some of the tasks in the list of Eloundou et al. (2023) are

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: hard-to-learn, where productivity gains may be significantly less than those based on

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: the experimental studies that have focused on the easy-to-learn tasks.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: In the next subsection, I make a preliminary attempt at incorporating the third possi-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: bility, but I will ignore the first two. Nevertheless, these considerations make me conclude

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: that even the 0.66% increase in TFP within the next 10 years due to AI is likely to be an

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: upper bound on this technology’s medium-run effects.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote:
3.3
Aggregate Productivity Gains: Incorporating Hard Tasks

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: In this subsection, I refine the estimates from the previous subsection by switching to equa-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: tion (15), which can be rewritten as:

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote:
TFP gains
=
GDP share of impacted easy tasks × average cost savings from easy tasks

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 32 页
sources.quote: +GDP share of impacted hard tasks × average cost savings from hard tasks.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: I take the 27% labor cost savings, from Noy and Zhang (2023) and Brynjolfsson et al.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: (2023), to apply to easy-to-learn tasks. The discussion in the previous section suggests that

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: most hard tasks have not been impacted or automated yet, and hence it is impossible to

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: know what their cost savings will be. Here I take those productivity gains to be 7%. My

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: reasoning is as follows. I consider the tasks involved in the Peng et al. (2023) study to be

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: very easy-to-learn for generative AI for reasons explained above. Those studied in Noy and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: Zhang (2023) are also on the easy side, and led to cost savings of about 40%, which is about

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: two thirds of the cost savings in Peng et al., while the customer service tasks in Brynjolfsson

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: et al. (2023) are already moving towards somewhat more complex tasks, and these had cost

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: savings of only 14%. I imagine that many of the hard-to-learn tasks are more challenging for

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: AI models than the simpler end of the customer service tasks to which Brynjolfsson et al.’s

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: numbers refer. This motivates my choice of half of the cost savings of their study, 7% (which

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: is also about a quarter of the baseline 27% cost reduction estimate I used in the previous

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: subsection).

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: The cost-saving numbers for both easy and hard tasks are again multiplied with 0.535

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: to convert them into overall cost savings—0.144 and 0.037 for easy and hard tasks, respec-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: tively. To obtain the shares of easy and hard tasks, I start from Eloundou et al.’s data and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: methodology, and then develop a procedure, implemented using GPT-4 like they do, for

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: sorting these into easy and hard tasks. The key characteristic for easy tasks is the presence

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: of a well-observed outcome and a straightforward rule that links actions/recommendations

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: to characteristics of the problem at hand.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: To implement this procedure, I start from the 4089 exposed tasks determined from the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: above procedure. Each one of these tasks has a statement on O*NET that includes at least

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: one verb. Each task also belongs to the higher level of aggregation of Detailed Work Activites

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: (DWAs) and the (even coarser) 332 Intermediate Work Activities (IWAs). The procedure

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: proceeds in four steps:

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: 1. Classification of verbs: Each task statement includes at least one verb which is

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: located at the beginning and can be easily identified. These primary verbs describe

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: much of what is “hard” or “easy” that needs to be learned about the task. We classified

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: tasks manually into easy and hard categories.25 The full list of tasks is provided in the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: Appendix. As an illustration, verbs for easy tasks include, among others: compute,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: resolve, count, draft, grade, transcribe, classify, standardize, write, and record. Many

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 33 页
sources.quote: 25This step and other manual coding steps in this subsection were carried out by Can Ye¸sildere.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: of these verbs are associated with simple actions that follow a clear set of steps and also

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: implicitly have a well-defined metric for success (such as accounting or grading). In

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: contrast, verbs for hard tasks include: participate, advise, instruct, diagnose, educate,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: hire, represent, testify, and care. The latter set of verbs describes more open-ended

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: activities for which there is less likely to be a clear metric of success. Yet other verbs,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: such as analyze, maintain or inspect, do not fall into either of these categories, and are

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: coded as “uncertain”.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: 2. Classification of IWAs: IWAs provide additional context for verbs, especially for

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: actions that verbs alone lack. We manually classify the 332 IWAs into easy and hard

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote:
tasks.
Some of the easy IWAs are: Evaluate project feasibility; Maintain sales or

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: financial records; Explain regulations, policies, or procedures; Issue documentation;

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: and Teach safety procedures or standards to others. Some of the hard ones include:

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: Monitor health conditions of humans or animals; Evaluate scholarly work; Evaluate

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: the quality or accuracy of data; Maintain safety or security; and Train animals. These

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: examples highlight the same principle mentioned in the discussion of verbs—easy-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: to-learn activities are those for which there is a clear metric of success and simple

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: rules that can achieve this successful outcome, while these are absent in hard-to-learn

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: activities.26

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: 3. Latent Dirichlet Allocation (LDA) topic modeling: While tasks may share

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: IWAs and verbs, each task is also worded uniquely to capture the subject and the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: more detailed description of activities. While “writing an audit report” and “writing a

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: letter of recommendation” are both associated with the same verb and the same IWA,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: the content and skills required for these tasks are different. To better disambiguate the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: contexts of these tasks, we use the LDA to allocate tasks into clusters. LDA procedure

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: is unsupervised and clusters tasks using the co-occurence matrices of words extracted

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: from each task statement. It assigns a probability to each task belonging to a topic

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: cluster (Blei et al., 2003). We feed all 19, 281 tasks into the algorithm and use LDA

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: to identify 100 clusters and the probability that each task belongs to one of those 100

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: clusters.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote: 4. Final assignment: The final step of our procedure is to derive a probability that

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 34 页
sources.quote:
26Of course, there is considerable ambiguity in some cases. For example, “Maintain safety and security”
also includes IT security activities, such as making sure that a new password can be issued to an authorized
person, and this would be an easy-to-learn task. The third step is aimed at dealing with such ambiguities.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: each exposed task is easy or hard. We first manually classify a random sample of 500

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: exposed tasks as easy or hard. We then use the classification of verbs, classification of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: IWAs, and the LDA-derived probabilities to train a gradient-boosted tree (Friedman,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: 2001) to match the manual classifications of the training sample of tasks. We finally

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: obtain a probabilistic assignment of each one of the 4089 exposed tasks into easy or

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: hard task category from this algorithm.27

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: The end result is that 72.6% of wage bill-weighted exposed tasks in Eloundou et al.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: are easy. This means that easy exposed tasks comprise 3.3% of GDP, while the remaining

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: exposed tasks (making up 1.3% of GDP) are hard. Incorporating this information together

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: with the assumptions on cost savings yields the following tighter upper bound on TFP gains

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: in the next 10 years:

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote:
TFP gains over the next 10 years
=
0.033 × 0.144 + (0.046 −0.033) × 0.037

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: Unsurprisingly, this is smaller than the estimate in the previous subsection. Since automating

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: hard-to-learn tasks—and even more so, introducing task complementarities for them—will

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: be more challenging, I view this estimate to be more reasonable. Either way, the TFP gains

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: within the next 10 years appear quite modest.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote:
3.4
From TFP to GDP

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: Given the TFP effects of AI over the 10 year horizon, the total GDP effects of AI over the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: same horizon can be computed from equation (13). Namely, this equation can be written as:

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote:
GDP gains over the next 10 years
=
TFP gains over the next 10 years

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: + capital share × proportional increase in capital stock.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: As a simple benchmark, I start by assuming that the capital stock will grow proportion-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: ately with TFP, which implies:

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote: GDP gains over the next 10 years = TFP gains over the next 10 years /(1−capital share).

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 35 页
sources.quote:
27As examples, the algorithm assigns a probability of 0.98 that “Maintaining equipment service records”
is an easy task, while only a probability of 0.098 that “Interviewing credit card applicants by telephone or
in person” is an easy task. Because writing and drafting are classified as verbs associated with easy tasks,
activities that involve writing are classified generally as easy. Some of this may understate the difficulty
of some writing-related tasks. For example, “Writing reports or academic papers to communicate findings
of climate-related studies” is classified to be an easy task with probability 0.67, which is likely to be an
underestimate of how hard such a task will continue to be for AI in the foreseeable future.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: Using the capital share for the entire private business sector, 0.43, this implies that GDP

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: gains will be equal to the TFP gains multiplied by 1.75 (≃1/(1 −0.43)). Hence taking the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: baseline estimate of an increase in TFP of 0.66%, I obtain a first estimate for GDP growth

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: due to AI of 1.16% over 10 years, or taking the presence of hard tasks into account, a lower

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: estimate of 0.93%.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote:
3.5
Consequences of New Bad Tasks

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: The calculations so far leave out the effects of new tasks introduced thanks to AI (and equiv-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: alently, the system-wide adjustments that AI may enable in some businesses, as emphasized

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: by Bresnahan (2019) and Agrawal et al. (2023). It is even more challenging to put numbers

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: on the effects of new tasks. If AI helps create new tasks that increase productivity and espe-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: cially contributes to the reinstatement of workers of different skill levels into the production

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: process, its consequences can be much more positive.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: Here my purpose is simply to point out that in the case of AI, because some of the new

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: tasks may be of the “bad” type, there may be an overstatement of the welfare gains from

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: AI when we look at GDP numbers. As an extremely preliminary attempt to argue that this

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: could be important, I will draw on two sources of data.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: The first is the recent study by Bursztyn et al. (2023), which provides suggestive esti-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: mates for the extent of this problem in the case of social media. Bursztyn et al. (2023) run

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: an experiment to evaluate the welfare effects of social media for college students, the demo-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: graphic group most engaged with social media. They ask TikTok and Instagram users how

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: much they would need to be paid to not use the platform for a month. Users of these two

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: platforms are willing to pay up to $59 and $47 a month, respectively, to continue to use social

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: media—or on average $53 per user-month. However, they find that users are also willing

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: to pay $28 and $10 every month to get everyone from their social network off TikTok and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: Instagram, respectively—or an average $19 per user-month. If non-users are also included in

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: the analysis, the willingness to pay to stop everybody using social media increases to $47 for

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: TikTok and $13 for Instagram. This suggests that while companies can profitably market

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: AI-based social media, the net effect on welfare may be negative. Quantitatively, I ignore

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: the non-users (since the population in the study is college students, who are more likely to be

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 36 页
sources.quote: impacted by social media activity even when they do not use it than the adult population in

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: the United States). I also start with a benchmark in which AI-powered platforms can capture

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: the full (average) $53 willingness to pay per user (for example, because they are effectively

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: price discriminating by varying the intensity with which they are collecting and monetizing

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: users’ data). Then taking the average between the two platforms, I conclude that for every

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: $53 of revenue, there is a net negative effect on users of $19. Put differently, the total effect

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: from this class of new bad tasks, the equivalent of (18) in theory, is −19/53 ≃−0.36 in

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: proportionate terms. Note also that if I assumed instead that social media companies can

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: capture less than the full $53 per user-month, then the denominator in this expression would

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: be smaller, and thus the proportionate damage per dollar of revenue would be higher.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: I combine the number −0.36 with estimates of (i) revenues from social media and digital

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: ads, and (ii) spending on malicious IT attacks and IT security against these attacks to

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: compute apparent and real gains from new bad tasks. Specifically, the total revenues in 2022

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: of Meta (Facebook plus Instagram), Alphabet (Google and Youtube), Snapchat, TikTok and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: Twitter (“X”) comes to 460 billion, or about 1.64% of US GDP,28 while a lower bound on IT

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: security is 78 billion or 0.28% of US GDP.29 Assuming that spending by malicious actors on

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: IT attacks is at least one third of this and combining these three estimates, I arrive to 2% of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: US GDP. This number could be a significant underestimate of other manipulative activities

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: enabled by new AI technologies. On the other hand, it could also overstate the problem, since

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: only a fraction of digital ad revenues will come from such manipulative activities (and this

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: may be particularly true for digital ad revenues from Google search). These considerations

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: suggest that the numbers here should be taken as merely suggestive.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: Taking the 2% of US GDP as revenues from new bad tasks and using the numbers from

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: Bursztyn et al. (2023) suggests that the total negative effects of these manipulative activities

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: is 0.02 × 0.36 = 0.072% of GDP (in consumption equivalent units). This number points to a

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: sizable negative impact on welfare, and could be larger if manipulative uses of generative AI

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: becomes more widespread. In contrast, if one were to simply count the revenue coming from

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: these new tasks, one might conclude that they would increase GDP by 2%. This discussion

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: thus suggests caution in interpreting all increases in GDP coming from the use of generative

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 37 页
sources.quote: AI as a positive effect on consumer welfare.

30If there were task complementarities, this would increase the productivity of exposed demographic groups
in the remaining subtasks, but would also reduce the automation-driven cost savings by a corresponding
amount. If task complementarities and automation affected different demographic groups within occupations
symmetrically, this would have minor effects on the conclusions: although the wage effects of productivity
gains from task complementarities are a little different than the cost savings generated by automation
(Acemoglu and Restrepo, 2022), the results would remain broadly similar. If, on the other hand, some groups
benefited more from task complementarities (for example, because they are overrepresented among middle-
expertise workers that can benefit most from generative AI tools), the distributional consequences could be
different. Since I do not have a way of distinguishing productivity effects from task complementarities and
automation, I am unable to explore this issue further.
