sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: wages as a result of AI.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: Overall, this exercise suggests that the inequality consequences of AI will not be as

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: adverse as pre-AI automation, because AI exposure is more equally distributed across de-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: mographic groups. Nevertheless, there is no evidence that AI will reduce inequality, as some

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: are forecasting. Rather, my analysis suggests that it may have a small positive effect on

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: overall (between-group) inequality and reduce the real earnings of low-education women. It

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: will also further widen the gap between capital and labor income.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote:
4
Concluding Remarks and Discussion

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: Following its release on November 30, 2022, ChatGPT became the fastest spreading tech plat-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: form in history, reaching approximately 100 million monthly users within just two months.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: Its impressive features, and the greater capabilities of the newer version ChatGPT-4, released

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: in March 2023, soon captured imaginations, both among the general public and economic

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: commentators. Forecasts of large productivity gains have now become commonplace.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: While there is no question that generative AI models, including ChatGPT, have impres-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: sive achievements and have great potential for beneficial economic effects, the extent of their

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: macroeconomic consequences remains an open question.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: There are four potential types of macro effects that AI technologies can have in the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: medium run:

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: 1. They can quickly revolutionize every aspect of the economy, and lead to massive im-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote:
provements in productivity, even taking us close to “singularity”.
While this is a

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: possibility that cannot be completely ruled out, there is so far no evidence of such

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: revolutionary effects (Nordhaus, 2021), and these are not addressed in the current

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: 2. They can have more modest but still notable effects on the macroeconomy by improving

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: productivity and reducing costs in a range of tasks. Some of the forecasts have focused

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: on these types of improvements and still produced relatively large numbers, such as a

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: 1.5 −3.4 percentage point per annum increase in economic growth within a 10 year

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: horizon.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: 3. They can impact wages and inequality because of their automation effects, or con-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: versely, lead to large wage increases, especially for lower-pay workers, as forecast by

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 44 页
sources.quote: The Economist (2023).

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: 4. They can have macroeconomic effects by producing deepfakes, misinformation, manip-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: ulation and other “bads”.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: In this paper, I use the task-based framework of Acemoglu and Restrepo (2018, 2019b,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: 2022) to evaluate the second and the third effects, and I also take some steps to formalize

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: how the fourth set of effects might work out in a task-based macro framework.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: I base my approach on existing experimental studies that estimate productivity gains and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: time savings from the use of generative AI tools in a number of settings. By building on these

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: studies, I am explicitly taking on board the idea that generative AI will lead to productivity

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: improvements. Nevertheless, combining these numbers with estimates of exposed tasks from

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: Eloundou et al. (2023) and Svanberg et al. (2024) leads to much more modest productivity

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: effects than most commentators and economists have claimed so far. These numbers become

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: even smaller once we take into account that many of the tasks for which we have evidence of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: cost savings are relatively easy for AI, while in several other tasks the integration of AI will

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: face more formidable difficulties—mostly because these are likely to involve more complex

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: interactions between action and context and because they lack clear metrics for success that

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: are observable, and hence necessitate AI models to learn from the (average) behavior of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: humans previously performing the same tasks.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: Taking these considerations into account, I estimate that TFP effects from AI advances

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: within the next 10 years will be modest—an upper bound that does not take into account

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: the distinction between hard and easy tasks would be about a 0.66% increase in total within

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: 10 years, or about a 0.064% increase in annual TFP growth. When the presence of hard

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: tasks among those that will be exposed to AI is recognized, this upper bound drops to

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: about 0.53%. GDP effects will be somewhat larger than this because automation and task

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: complementarities will also lead to greater investment. But my calculations suggest that the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: GDP boost within the next 10 years should also be modest, in the range of 0.93% −1.16%

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: over 10 years in total, provided that the investment increase resulting from AI is modest,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: and in the range of 1.4% −1.56% in total, if there is a large investment boom.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: If AI is used to create new tasks and products, these will also add to GDP and can

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote:
boost productivity growth.
Nevertheless, when we incorporate the possibility that new

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: tasks generated by AI may be manipulative, the impact on welfare can be even smaller.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: Based on numbers from Bursztyn et al. (2023), which pertain to the negative effects of AI-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: powered social media, I provide an illustrative calculation for social media, digital ads and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 45 页
sources.quote: IT defense-attack spending. These could add to GDP by as much as 2%, but if we apply

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: the numbers from Bursztyn et al. (2023), their impact on welfare may be −0.72%. This

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: discussion suggests that it is important to consider the potential negative implications of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: AI-generated new tasks and products on welfare.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: Finally, I borrow heavily from the estimates of Acemoglu and Restrepo (2022) on the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: economy-wide productivity, wage and inequality effects of pre-AI automation technologies

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: to provide some guidance on what the impact of new AI advances will be. Because AI-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: exposed tasks are more equally distributed within the population than tasks exposed to

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: pre-AI automation, I do not find substantial negative wage effects for any education group.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: Nevertheless, the estimates do not point to significant reductions in inequality either, and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: in fact, my findings suggest that low-education women may experience small wage declines,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: overall between-group inequality may increase slightly, and the gap between capital and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: labor income is likely to widen further.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: These results should not be interpreted as arguing that there are no major benefits from

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: AI. First, an increase of about 0.53 −0.66% in TFP within 10 years is modest but still far

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: from trivial. Second and more importantly, there may be other ways in which AI can be used

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: to generate much more notable benefits. I have suggested in previous work (Acemoglu, 2021,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: Acemoglu and Restrepo, 2020b) that if AI is used for generating new tasks for workers, it can

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: have more beneficial productivity, wage and inequality consequences, and it can even increase

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: wages. This may be doubly true for generative AI, which could be used for providing better

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: information to workers and boosting their expertise, as argued in Acemoglu et al. (2023)

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: and explained briefly here.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: Many production workers today, including electricians, repair workers, plumbers, nurses,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: educators, clerical workers, and increasingly many blue-collar workers in factories, are en-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: gaged in problem-solving tasks. These tasks require real-time, context-dependent and reli-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: able information. For instance, an electrician dealing with the malfunctioning of advanced

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: equipment or a short-circuit on the electricity grid will be hampered from solving these prob-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: lems because he or she does not have sufficient expertise and the appropriate information

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: for troubleshooting. Reliable information that can be provided quickly by generative AI

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: tools can lead to significant improvements in productivity. Similarly, generative AI in class-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: rooms can lead to a major reorganization of how teaching takes place, with greater levels

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: of personalization, as these tools help teachers identify specific aspects of the curriculum

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: with which subgroups of students are having problems and propose new context-dependent

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 46 页
sources.quote: teaching strategies. Reliability of AI models will be key for successfully creating such new

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: tasks and delivering improvements in the quality of education.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: Productivity improvements from new tasks and new products, which have been impor-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: tant for previous transformative technologies, such as electricity and the Internet, are not

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: incorporated into my estimates. This is for three reasons. First and most parochially, this is

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: much harder to measure and is not included in the types of exposure considered in Eloundou

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: et al. (2023) and Svanberg et al. (2024). Second, and more importantly, I believe it is right

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: not to include these in the likely macroeconomic effects, because these are not the areas

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: receiving attention from the industry at the moment, as also argued in Acemoglu (2021),

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: Acemoglu and Restrepo (2020b) and Acemoglu and Johnson (2023). Rather, areas of pri-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: ority for the tech industry appear to be around automation and monetization of personal

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: data, such as through search or social media digital ads. This makes it less likely that many

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: new good tasks will be created quickly.Third, and relatedly, more beneficial outcomes may

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: require new institutions, policies and regulations, as also suggested in Acemoglu and Johnson

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: (2023) and Acemoglu et al. (2023).

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: My assessment is that there are indeed much bigger gains to be had from generative AI,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: which is a promising technology, but these gains will remain elusive unless there is a funda-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: mental reorientation of the industry, including perhaps a major change in the architecture

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: of the most common generative AI models, such as the LLMs, in order to focus on reliable

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: information that can increase the marginal productivity of different kinds of workers, rather

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: than prioritizing the development of general human-like conversational tools. The general-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: purpose nature of the current approach to generative AI could be ill-suited for providing

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: such reliable information. To put it simply, it remains an open question whether we need

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: foundation models (or the current kind of LLMs) that can engage in human-like conver-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: sations and write Shakespearean sonnets if what we want is reliable information useful for

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 47 页
sources.quote: educators, healthcare professionals, electricians, plumbers and other craft workers.

A-1
Exposed Share of Tasks

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: Eloundou et al. (2023) present task-level exposures estimates based on O*NET, which lists

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: tasks by occupation at the level of the eight-digit Standard Occupational Classification

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: (SOC). We link thess data to the BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: (OEWS) for 2019 to 2022 to calculate the wage bill-weighted share of exposed tasks in

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: the economy. BLS OEWS data are reported at the six-digit SOC level, and we combine

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: these two sources of data as follows:

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: 1. Six-digit direct matching: We compute occupational exposures scores at the eight-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: digit SOC level based on Eloundou et al. (2023). We then aggregate these eight-digit

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: numbers to the six-digit SOC level (with equal weights). This direct match covers

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: 90.8% of the total wage bill in the economy.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: 2. Aggregation to five-digit: In this step, we aggregate the six-digit SOC occupations

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: to five-digits. For five-digit occupations that include both six-digit occupations with

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: exposure estimates and wage bill information in BLS OEWS, we compute the wage

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: bill share-weighted average of the six-digit occupations. This weighting scheme ensures

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: that the information at the six-digit level is preserved when we aggregate up to five-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: digits. BLS OEWS does not report wage bill information for some small occupations,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: and as a result, for some five-digit occupations we have no direct match to six-digit

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: occupations with exposure and wage bill data. In such cases, we compute the five-digit

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: exposure by taking the unweighted average of all corresponding six-digit occupations

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: with exposure data. These steps together cover 99.3% of the total wage bill in the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: economy. The remaining five-digit occupations, which make up 0.7% of the wage bill

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: and have no exposure information in Eloundou et al. (2023), are assumed to have zero

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 52 页
sources.quote: exposure. This aggregated occupational exposure score is denoted by Γ0.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote:
A-3
Easy and Hard Tasks

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: The procedure used for classifying “easy-to-learn” (or “easy”) and “hard-to-learn” (or

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: “hard”) tasks is described at a high level in the text. Here I provide further details.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: We start with Eloundou et al’s exposure measure and focus on three features of tasks (i)

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: primary verbs, (ii) IWAs, and (iii) topic clusters coded by LDA.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: 1. Primary verbs: Each task on O*NET has a task description that starts with at

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: least one verb. These “primary” verbs are informative about what the task involves

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: and how easily a task can be automated using AI. In particular, verbs that indicate

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: objective measurement possibilities for the outcome (e.g., calculate or quantify) or

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: involve predictable rules that allow for easy mapping to outcomes (estimate) are more

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: likely to be associated with easy tasks.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: We manually classified verbs as easy, hard or uncertain, where the last category con-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: tains verbs that are harder to classify or involve both harder and easier elements (for

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: which the context will be important as I describe next). The full list of verbs and their

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: classifications are provided in the replication package, and the most common hard and

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: easy verbs are listed in Table A-1 in this Appendix.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: 2. Intermediate Work Activities: Each task on O*NET is situated within a hierarchy

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: and is associated with at least one Detailed Work Activity (DWA), which is a coarser

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: description of the task. Each DWA is in turn associated with at least one Intermediate

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: Work Activity (IWA), which is at a higher level aggregation. There are 19264 tasks

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: and 332 IWAs in O*NET. While verbs are informative on whether the observed act is

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: associated with a predictable outcome, IWAs provide context about the observability of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: the outcome. For example, explaining can be hard-to-learn when it is in the context of

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: teaching key concepts to elementary school students, but easy-to-learn when it involves

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: explaining the rules of a parlor game. We manually classified each IWA as easy or hard

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: taking this context into account. The replication package also includes the exact list

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: of IWA classifications.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: 3. Topic clusters: We use a separate unsupervised learning algorithm, the Latent Dirich-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: let Allocation (LDA) algorithm (Blei et al., 2003), to determine probabilistic topic

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: clusters. Topic clusters provide an additional layer of context for the algorithm. We

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 54 页
sources.quote: apply the LDA algorithm to all 19264 tasks to generate 100 topic clusters. LDA lever-

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: ages word co-occurence within task statements to determine probabilistic assignment

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: of each task to topic clusters.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: We use the output of these three steps with our supervised learning model, which is a

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: gradient boosted classifier (GBC) (Friedman, 2001). GBCs maximize goodness-of-fit over a

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: training set by iteratively generating partitions. We produce the training set by manually

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: classifying 757 of the 4089 exposed tasks. The GBC produces the best fit for these 757 tasks,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: and we obtain the output of the classifier for the remaining tasks. The inputs into the GBC

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: are: the verb classification, the IWA classification, and probabilities to belonging to each

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: one of the 100 topic clusters from the LDA. In addition, we also feed the GBC the empirical

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: frequencies of each verb being associated with an easy or uncertain task (hard task being the

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: omitted category), and each IWA being associated with an easy task in our training data.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: This information is useful as it provides an empirical measure of the degree of certainty with

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: which each verb and IWA is classified (analogous to the prior in a Bayesian calculation).

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: When a task has more than one primary verb, we take the average across these.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: The goodness-of-fit of the GBC is quite good. It matches 90% of the manual classification

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: on our training data and has an AUC (area under the curve) score of 0.99. As output, we

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: generate the probability of each task being easy-to-learn or hard-to-learn. When calculating

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: the adjusted TFP scores, we weight each task by the degree of exposure (according to

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: Eloundou et al) multiplied by the probability scores, to obtain the share of easy-to-learn

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: tasks in the economy. Further details on the GBC and the training sample are contained in

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: the replication package.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: Finally, it is important to note that because the GBC algorithm is trained and tested

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: exclusively on exposed tasks, its output is most meaningful for this sample. For example, for

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: verbs that are absent or rare in this sample, it would not provide a meaningful classification.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: Therefore, its output should not be directly extrapolated to non-exposed tasks. Moreover,

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: because Eloundou et al’s sample is already for exposed tasks, we would expect a higher

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: fraction of these to be easy-to-learn than for the entire set of tasks. Indeed, as reported

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: in the text, about three quarters of the wage bill-weighted exposed tasks are classified as

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: easy-to-learn within this sample.

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote:
A-4
Wage and Inequality Calculations

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: To estimate the general equilibrium impact of AI on wage outcomes, I follow the methodology

sources.title: macroeconomics-ai · 第 55 页
sources.quote: used in Acemoglu and Restrepo (2022).

visuals.description: Figure 1 shows the distribution of AI exposure (feasible AI exposure %) across the wage distribution for 500 demographic groups, with marker size proportional to employment level and color indicating education level. The horizontal axis is average hourly wage (2018–2022, log scale, 2020 dollars); vertical axis is feasible AI exposure (%). The figure illustrates that higher-wage groups tend to have higher AI exposure, but there is substantial overlap across education levels.

visuals.description: Figure 2 shows a four-panel scatter plot decomposition of AI-induced wage effects (2018–2022) by education level (Less than high school, High school, Some college, College, Postgraduate), with marker sizes proportional to average employment levels. Panel A: productivity effect only. Panel B: adds industry shifts. Panel C: adds direct task displacement. Panel D: adds ripple effects. Horizontal axis: log-scale hourly wage in 2018–2022 (2020 dollars). Vertical axis: estimated wage change (range approx. -0.15 to +0.15). The figure is based on propagation matrix estimates from Acemoglu and Restrepo (2022) combined with exposure to easy/hard AI tasks.
